q: What material neutralizes acid liquid waste?
n: Acid wastes from laboratories are passed through a neutralizing tank filled with limestone (calcium carbonate) chips, which raise the pH before discharge. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (chemical wastes); Uniform Plumbing Code Sec. 811.

q: How is the size of a sewage pit determined?
o: By the volume of storm water
By the volume of liquid waste
By the volume of solid waste
By the volume of solid, liquid, and storm waste
n: A sewage pit (septic chamber) is sized by the volume of solid waste it must hold between desludgings, as well as detention time. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (septic tank capacity).

q: In a location where there is no provision for a drainage line, what is the next best solution?
o: Use drain tiles connected to an open field
Store waste in a tank and dispose of it in a sanitary landfill
n: Where no public sewer exists, treated effluent is dispersed through perforated drain tiles laid in an open leaching (absorption) field. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (disposal fields); US EPA Onsite Wastewater Treatment Systems Manual.

q: Where are storm sewers typically located?
o: Under the sidewalk on narrow roads and under the roadway on wide roads
At the center of the road
n: Storm sewers run near the curb, where the gutter inlets and catch basins collect street runoff. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines (drainage); utility placement standards.

q: Which type of pipe is NOT suitable for underground use?
n: Galvanized iron pipe corrodes in contact with soil and moisture, so it is not suitable underground without protection. PVC and clay pipes are made for burial. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (materials); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which sewage treatment step uses chlorine compounds to kill pathogens?
n: Disinfection is the treatment step that kills pathogens, most commonly by chlorination (or UV and ozone) before discharge. Source: Metcalf & Eddy, Wastewater Engineering; DENR effluent standards (DAO 2016-08).

q: Which should NOT pass through a structural beam?
n: Large soil pipes passing through a structural beam would cut away much of its section and cannot be serviced. Small sleeved conduits and pipes are allowed only per the structural engineer's design. Source: NSCP 2015 (openings in beams); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which best describes blackwater?
o: Wastewater from showers, sinks and laundry
n: Blackwater is wastewater containing human waste from toilets and urinals. Showers, sinks and laundry produce gray water. Source: US EPA terminology; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is liquid waste without urine, feces or industrial waste called?
n: Gray water is wastewater from sinks, showers, lavatories and laundry, without fecal matter or industrial waste. Source: US EPA terminology; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (gray water systems).

q: What is a watertight tank where sewage is held for treatment?
n: A septic tank is a watertight receptacle that holds sewage for settling and anaerobic digestion. A cesspool is not watertight. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions).

q: What is the minimum water level required in a septic tank?
n: A septic tank needs a minimum liquid depth of about 2 ft (600 mm), so solids can settle and scum can form properly. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (septic tank dimensions).

q: For a septic tank located on a rocky seashore and exposed during low tide, what waterproofing method is appropriate?
o: Waterproof all interior and exterior surfaces
Waterproof the interior except the floor
n: A septic tank in rock along a tidal shore is exposed to seawater on both sides as the tide changes, so all interior and exterior surfaces must be waterproofed to stop infiltration and leakage. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (watertight septic tanks); DOH sanitation guidelines.

q: Which of these is NOT usually installed underground?
n: A downspout (leader) runs down the face of the building from the gutter. Septic tanks, cisterns and manholes are underground structures. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (storm drainage).

q: Where is the worst place to lay a PVC pipe?
n: Beneath a tree is the worst place for a buried PVC pipe, because roots seek moisture, crack joints and clog the line. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is least appropriate next to a lobby?
n: A garbage chute brings odor, noise and pests, so it belongs in the service core, not next to a lobby. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (service areas); NBC IRR (refuse chutes).

q: What is the main job of a catch basin?
o: Collecting storm water and trapping debris
n: A catch basin collects surface storm water and has a sump below the outlet that traps sand, silt and debris before the water enters the drain line. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines (drainage); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is done before backfilling utility trenches?
o: Pressure test or inspect the lines
n: Utility lines are pressure-tested or inspected for leaks and grade before trenches are backfilled, while defects can still be reached. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (tests and inspections).

q: A commonly cited estimate (World Bank) puts the share of the Philippine population connected to a sewer network at about:
n: The World Bank estimates only about 5% of Filipinos are connected to a sewer network. Most households rely on septic tanks. Source: World Bank, Philippines Sanitation Sourcebook / Water and Sanitation Program reports.

q: What is the approximate percentage of households with access to piped sewerage systems in the Philippines?
n: DENR estimates that about 10% of Philippine households have access to piped sewerage systems. Source: DENR, National Water Quality Status Report.

q: Which is the largest chamber of a septic tank?
n: The first (digestion) chamber is the largest, about two-thirds of the tank volume. It is where solids settle and are digested. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (septic tank compartments).

q: Which of the following is a known brand and supplier of floor drains and manholes?
n: Jaman is a known Philippine brand and supplier of floor drains, cleanouts and manhole covers. Toto and Kohler are sanitary ware, and Delta is faucets. Source: Philippine plumbing supplier catalogs.

q: What follows the digestion chamber in a two-chamber septic tank?
n: In a two-chamber septic tank, effluent flows from the digestion chamber to the leaching (second) chamber before disposal. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (septic tanks); DOH sanitation guidelines.

q: What is the last part of a downspout?
n: A downspout discharges at its lower end into a catch basin (or a storm drain inlet), which traps debris before the storm drain. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (storm drainage).

q: What mainly determines gutter size?
o: Rainfall intensity and the roof area it falls on
n: A gutter is sized by the design rainfall intensity and the roof area draining into it, which together set the runoff it must carry. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (storm drain sizing tables); SMACNA gutter sizing.

q: What device, like a small septic tank, separates and holds grease from kitchen waste?
n: A grease trap (interceptor) is a small tank that slows kitchen waste so grease floats and is retained before the water goes to the sewer. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (grease interceptors).

q: What does a catch basin do in a storm drainage system?
o: Traps solid debris from storm water
Connects sewers to the septic tank
n: A catch basin traps sand, silt and litter in its sump so they do not clog the storm drain pipes. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines (drainage).

q: What keeps sewer odors from entering a building through the drainage system?
n: A trap's water seal stops sewer gases in the drainage system from entering the building through fixtures. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (traps).

q: MRF stands for:
n: MRF means Materials Recovery Facility, required by RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act) for sorting and recovering recyclables. Source: RA 9003, Sec. 32.

q: STP stands for:
n: STP means Sewage Treatment Plant, a facility that treats wastewater to DENR effluent standards before discharge. Source: DENR DAO 2016-08 (water quality guidelines and effluent standards).

q: What is the main purpose of a materials recovery facility?
n: A Materials Recovery Facility receives mixed waste and sorts, segregates, composts and recycles it, so only residuals go to disposal. Source: RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act), Sec. 32.

q: Which is a byproduct of sewage treatment?
n: Every sewage treatment process produces sludge, the settled and biological solids, which must be thickened, digested and disposed of. Source: Metcalf & Eddy, Wastewater Engineering.

q: What is the first stage of sewage treatment?
n: Treatment begins with preliminary treatment: bar screens and grit chambers remove rags, coarse solids and sand before primary settling. Source: Metcalf & Eddy, Wastewater Engineering.

q: What drain fitting is used in kitchen and laundry sinks?
n: A basket strainer is the sink drain fitting with a removable basket that catches food scraps in kitchen and laundry sinks. Source: ASME A112.18.2 (waste fittings); plumbing fixture manufacturer literature.

q: What isn't needed per house when a subdivision has a sewage treatment plant?
n: When a subdivision has a central sewage treatment plant, each house's sewage goes to the STP through the sewer network, so individual septic tanks are not needed. Source: PD 957 and BP 220 IRR (sewage disposal); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What trap may be fitted in the building drain to keep sewer gas out?
n: A house (building) trap is a running trap installed in the building drain near where it leaves the building, keeping sewer gas from the public sewer out of the building. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (building traps).

q: Which fixture is designed to separate grease and fat from kitchen wastewater before the drain?
n: A grease trap (interceptor) separates and retains grease and fat from kitchen wastewater before it enters the drain. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (grease interceptors).

q: What keeps foul odors from rising through a floor drain?
n: The trap seal (the water standing in the floor drain's trap) blocks sewer gases. Floor drains in dry areas need trap primers to keep the seal from evaporating. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (traps).
